summary: College Park Airport (CGS) is one of the world's oldest continuously operating airports, established in 1909 when the U.S. Army Signal Corps selected the site for the nation's first military aviation training program, conducted by the Wright Brothers. Located just outside Washington, D.C., in Prince George's County, Maryland, it remains an active general aviation facility known for its historic significance and connection to early powered flight. The airport serves as a hub for flight training, recreational flying, and hosts annual events celebrating its aviation heritage.
faqs:
Q: What is the historical significance of College Park Airport?
A: College Park Airport is the world's oldest continuously operating airport, dating back to 1909 when the Wright Brothers trained the first U.S. military pilots there. It is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

Q: Does College Park Airport offer commercial flights?
A: No, CGS is a general aviation airport serving private pilots, flight schools, and recreational flying. There are no scheduled commercial airline services.

Q: Can visitors tour the airport?
A: Yes, the College Park Aviation Museum, located adjacent to the airport, offers exhibits about early aviation and the Wright Brothers. The museum and airport grounds are open to the public.

Q: What facilities are available for pilots?
A: The airport offers a single runway, tie-downs, hangar space, fuel services, and flight school operations through the College Park Aviation Museum's pilot training programs.
transport_tips: College Park Airport is easily accessed via the Baltimore-Washington Parkway (MD-295) and is approximately a 10-minute drive from the College Park metro station on the Washington Metro Green Line. Free parking is available on-site for visitors and pilots. Taxi and rideshare services like Uber and Lyft are readily available in the Washington, D.C. metropolitan area.
local_tip: Plan your visit around the annual open house events hosted by the College Park Aviation Museum, where you can see vintage aircraft fly, meet active pilots, and watch demonstrations—a rare treat at a working historic airport so close to the nation's capital.
